expectedFacts: FsmonitorSettings::from_settings turns the backend setting into Watchman, None, or an error for the test-only backend.

CRITICAL: TreeState::snapshot builds its scan matcher from make_fsmonitor_matcher: the changed paths reported by Watchman become a FilesMatcher (plus a prefix matcher for the directory of any changed .gitignore) that is unioned with force-tracking and intersected with the sparse matcher.
query_changed_files sends the stored clock and excludes the .git and .jj directories.
CRITICAL: If Watchman reports a fresh instance, no path list is returned and the whole working copy is crawled; if the query fails, a warning is logged and a full scan runs with no clock.
The last clock lives in TreeState.watchman_clock and is saved in the tree-state file.
The stored clock is not advanced when the monitor reported no changed paths, nor when the scan found untracked or invalid-UTF-8 paths (unless the new clock is None).

The Git backend uses the all-zero object id of the repo's hash type as the root commit id; no real Git object backs it, and read_commit returns a synthesized empty root commit (make_root_commit) for that id.
CRITICAL: read_commit gives every Git commit that has no parents (including commits cut off by a shallow clone) the root commit as its parent.
CRITICAL: write_commit leaves the root parent out of the Git commit and rejects a merge commit that has the root as one of its parents.
Ref export (collect_changed_refs_to_export) marks a bookmark or tag that targets the root commit as failed with OnRootCommit.
reset_head leaves Git HEAD unborn when the working-copy commit's first parent is the root commit.
import_head_commits skips the root id when importing heads, and gc skips it when recreating the no-gc refs that keep commits alive.
finish_transaction calls try_reset_git_head, which calls git::reset_head; a failed HEAD update is only a warning.
CRITICAL: reset_head points Git HEAD at the first parent of the working-copy commit (unborn if that is the root) when it differs from the recorded value.

reset_head calls clear_operation_state when Git is mid-operation, deleting MERGE_HEAD, MERGE_MODE, MERGE_MSG, REVERT_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, BISECT_LOG and the rebase-merge, rebase-apply and sequencer directories.
CRITICAL: reset_index rewrites the Git index from the working-copy commit's parent tree, and update_intent_to_add_impl marks files added in the working-copy commit as intent-to-add.

finish_transaction then calls export_refs (export_some_refs), which writes changed local bookmarks and tags as Git branches and tags, and first detaches HEAD (in the main repo and linked worktrees) when HEAD is a symbolic ref to a ref that is being moved or deleted.

r3h-jj-11.query: Leaving aside commands whose purpose is to create, enter or move to a commit (including cloning, initialising a repository, adding a workspace and bisecting), in which situations does jj create a brand-new commit on its own and make it my working copy? Name each situation and the function that does it.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: snapshot_working_copy writes a new commit (holding the snapshotted changes) on top of the working-copy commit when files changed and the recorded working-copy commit is immutable, with a warning.
CRITICAL: finish_transaction writes a new empty commit on top of the working-copy commit when a command left it immutable, with a warning that it became immutable.
MutableRepo::update_wc_commits creates a new commit on the merged parents' tree when the working-copy commit was abandoned, and checks it out with edit().
import_git_head checks out a new commit on top of a Git HEAD that was moved outside jj (shared Git folder), via MutableRepo::check_out.
create_and_check_out_recovery_commit creates a recovery commit on top of the old working-copy commit during stale-working-copy recovery when the working copy's operation can no longer be read.

CRITICAL: Config layers from lowest to highest precedence are: defaults, system config, base environment variables, user config, repo config, workspace config, override environment variables, command-line arguments (documented on config_from_environment).
env_base_layer sets the editor from the visual-editor variable and otherwise from the general editor variable, so user and repo config override them.
CRITICAL: The pager environment variable is deliberately not read (comment in env_base_layer, issue 3502); only the jj-specific pager variable in env_overrides_layer sets the pager.
env_overrides_layer maps the jj-specific editor and pager variables above all config files.
Platform defaults come from unix.toml (editor nano) and windows.toml (pager set to the builtin pager, editor Notepad); misc.toml sets the default external pager otherwise.
The merge.same-change setting is read by MergeOptions::from_settings in tree_merge.rs and handed to the Store by the repo loader, which exposes it as Store::merge_options().same_change.

CRITICAL: Tree and file-content merging (tree_merge.rs, merged_tree.rs, tree.rs, files.rs merge_inner and resolve_diff_hunks) pass that value to resolve_trivial/trivial_merge in core/src/merge.rs, where Keep leaves the conflict and Accept resolves it.
CRITICAL: Bookmark and remote-ref merging (merge_ref_targets and merge_remote_refs in refs.rs) hard-codes SameChange::Accept and never consults the setting.
tree_merge.rs resolves executable bits and copy ids with SameChange::Accept regardless of the setting.
commit_from_git_without_root_parent takes the change ID from the commit's change-id extra header via extract_change_id_from_commit (reverse hex, exactly 16 bytes).
CRITICAL: Without a usable header, synthetic_change_id_from_git_commit_id derives the ID from the last 16 bytes of the commit id, in reverse order with the bits of each byte reversed.

CRITICAL: On import (import_head_commits and import_extra_metadata_entries_from_heads) the computed change ID is stored in the extra-metadata table keyed by commit id so that later rewrites do not assign a new one.
On read, deserialize_extras overrides the change ID with the stored value when the table has one.
The signature template keyword wraps CryptographicSignature, whose status, key and display call Commit::verification, which calls store.signer().verify with the commit id, signed data and signature.
CRITICAL: Signer::verify first returns a cached Verification for the commit id from an in-memory LRU cache of 100 entries.
On a miss it tries the main backend and then the other backends that report can_read for the signature, skipping results that are Unknown or an invalid-format error so that the next backend can try.
CRITICAL: A Good or Bad result is cached for the commit id; a backend error other than invalid format is returned without caching.

If no backend yields Good or Bad (every reading backend says Unknown, for example because the key is missing, or no backend can read the signature), Signer::verify caches and returns a plain Unknown; the branch meant to skip caching Unknown is effectively unreachable because Unknown results are skipped earlier.
The cache lives in the Signer inside the Store, so it is per process and every new jj invocation verifies again.
CRITICAL: get_updated_tree_value treats a tracked file as clean only if its FileState (type including executable bit, mtime and size) equals the recorded one (is_clean).
CRITICAL: It additionally requires the recorded file mtime to be strictly earlier than the tree-state file's own mtime (own_mtime); otherwise the file is re-read even when everything else matches.
own_mtime is set by update_own_mtime from the tree_state file's metadata when the state is read and just before it is saved, and falls back to 0 if unavailable.
The reason is that a file modified at the same moment as the state file may have changed after the state was written (racy-timestamp problem).
